factors.label: Weather severity
factors.methodology: Worst hourly driver across rain rate (AMS/Met Office), gusts (Beaufort), heat (NWS heat index), cold (Env. Canada wind chill), WMO weather codes and visibility (WMO/NWS fog) over the assessed period.
factors.explanation: Strong gusts 10.9 m/s (Sun 12:00 local, at the destination)

factors.label: Hazard severity
factors.methodology: Highest official severity (GDACS alert / USGS PAGER or magnitude class / cyclone wind buffer) among active hazards whose footprint touches the subject, or point hazards within the assessment radius.
factors.explanation: No active hazard affects this location during the assessed period

factors.label: Distance to hazard
factors.methodology: Minimum geodesic distance from the subject to any active hazard geometry (footprint or centroid); proximity = 1 − min(d, R)/R with R = assessment radius.
factors.explanation: M 5.4 - 20 km NW of Anamizu, Japan is 276.5 km from the location (measured to its reported centre (no footprint published))

notes: Point location only — true extent unknown

factors.label: Route exposure
factors.methodology: Route ∩ active hazard footprints (GeoPandas overlay, local AEQD CRS): exposed length / route length; exposed duration = route duration × exposed fraction.
factors.explanation: Route exposure applies to journeys, not to a destination overview

factors.label: Time factor
factors.methodology: Darkness share of the period (NOAA solar elevation), tropical-cyclone season of the basin, overlap with hazard validity periods and forecast lead time; rule-based class.
factors.explanation: Sun 22 Nov 11:40 – Sun 22 Nov 12:40: Inside the Western North Pacific tropical-cyclone season (JMA climatology (main season))

factors.label: Historical incident risk
factors.methodology: Annual rate λ of significant hazard events (GDACS Orange/Red, USGS M≥6) within the historical radius over the window; P(≥1) = 1 − exp(−λt); class by return period. Verified TravelSphere incidents as a separate rate.
factors.explanation: 1 significant event within 150 km since 2016 (1 cyclone) — about 0.10/year, i.e. a 9.5% chance of at least one in a year

notes: Incident reports not normalised: visitor numbers unavailable

factors.label: Population exposure
factors.methodology: Locality population (GeoNames) counted as exposed when inside an affecting hazard (class ≥ moderate); class by order of magnitude (GDACS tiers). Travellers exposed and traveller-hours reported separately.
factors.explanation: No resident population exposed — Kyoto is outside every active hazard area (population 1,463,723)

notes: Population is the GeoNames locality total; density unavailable
